new.title: Explore the Castle of St Peter and its shipwreck museum
new.desc: The Knights Hospitaller built the castle from 1402 on the harbour headland, reusing stones from the Mausoleum. Since 1962 it houses the Museum of Underwater Archaeology, with finds such as the Uluburun shipwreck.
new.tip: Restoration has been under way since 2017, so only some halls are open; the castle ticket covers the museum. Go early in summer for shade and sea views from the towers.
new.q: Bodrum Kalesi, Kale Cd., Merkez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Stand on the site of the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus
new.desc: This tomb of Mausolus and Artemisia II, built in the 350s BC, was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Earthquakes toppled it and the Knights used its blocks for the castle; only foundations and a small museum remain.
new.tip: Little is left to see, so read about it first; the best sculptures are in the British Museum. Allow about 30 minutes.
new.q: Halikarnas Mausoleumu, Turgutreis Cd., Merkez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Sit in the 4th-century BC theatre above Bodrum
new.desc: The ancient theatre of Halicarnassus was cut into the hillside in the 4th century BC and looks over the harbour and castle. It once hosted gladiator shows and today stages summer concerts.
new.tip: Come at sunset for the view; the stones get hot in July and August. Check the Bodrum culture calendar for concerts.
new.q: Bodrum Antik Tiyatro, Kıbrıs Şehitleri Cd., Merkez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Touch the Myndos Gate in the old city wall
new.desc: Built under Mausolus in the 4th century BC, the gate is the best-preserved remnant of the 7 km wall that once ringed Halicarnassus. A dry moat and towers still flank it.
new.tip: Free to visit and quick to see on the walk between the Mausoleum and the western town. Pair it with a sunset drink nearby.
new.q: Myndos Kapısı, Turgutreis Cd., Merkez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Climb to the Bodrum windmills for the bay view
new.desc: A row of white windmills stands on the ridge between Bodrum and Gümbet, dating to the 18th century when they ground flour. The hilltop looks over both bays and the castle.
new.tip: Go late afternoon, as the climb is very hot in July and August. It is a 20-minute downhill walk to the marina.
new.q: Bodrum Yel Değirmenleri, Gümbet Yolu, Merkez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Discover Bodrum's boatbuilding at the Maritime Museum
new.desc: A small museum in the old bazaar covers the town's seafaring, with scale models and a film on traditional Bodrum gulet building. It is spread over two floors in a restored building.
new.tip: Takes under an hour and sits right in the bazaar, so combine it with lunch. Open daily in summer, usually 9:00 to 19:00.
new.q: Bodrum Deniz Müzesi, Nazım Hikmet Sk., Çarşı, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Visit the house of singer Zeki Müren
new.desc: The two-storey seafront house where the singer Zeki Müren lived from 1980 until his death in 1996 opened as a museum in June 2000. It displays his stage costumes, photos, videos and documents.
new.tip: Closed on Mondays; check hours as sources differ. Allow 45 minutes.
new.q: Zeki Müren Sanat Müzesi, Zeki Müren Cd. No:11, Kumbahçe, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Watch the sunset over ancient Myndos in Gümüşlük
new.desc: Gümüşlük stands on Myndos, a Carian city that flourished in the 2nd and 1st centuries BC. Walls and foundations lie submerged in the bay, and Rabbit Island sits just offshore.
new.tip: Arrive an hour before sunset and walk the shore, then eat at the waterfront. The last dolmuş back to Bodrum leaves early, so check it.
new.q: Myndos Antik Kenti, Gümüşlük Mah., Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: See the restored Yalıkavak seafront windmill
new.desc: Yalıkavak's old windmill on the waterfront dates to 1859 and was restored in 2005. It recalls the village's pre-resort life of fishing and sponge diving.
new.tip: Quick stop on a harbour stroll; the wind is best on summer afternoons.
new.q: Yalıkavak Yel Değirmeni, Yalıkavak Sahil, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Walk among the Leleg walls of ancient Pedasa
new.desc: Pedasa was a Leleg settlement, one of eight cities attributed to that people, that resisted Persian incursions in the 6th century BC. Parts of its fortifications of large unworked stones survive, and life continued until the Middle Byzantine period.
new.tip: Excavations have run since 2007; wear sturdy shoes and bring water, as the site is on a rural hillside. Ask locally in Konacık for the track.
new.q: Pedasa Antik Kenti, Gökçeler, Konacık, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Admire the Corinthian columns of Euromos
new.desc: The Temple of Zeus Lepsynos at Euromos, 12 km from Milas, was built under Hadrian in the 2nd century AD. Sixteen Corinthian columns still stand among olive groves.
new.tip: Open roughly 8:30 to 19:00, varying by season. Combine it with Milas and Beçin in a half-day.
new.q: Euromos Antik Kenti, Selimiye Yolu, Milas, Muğla

new.title: Hike up to the sanctuary of Zeus at Labraunda
new.desc: Labraunda is a sacred site of Carian Zeus in the mountains north of Milas, developed by the Hekatomnid rulers including Mausolus. Terraced courtyards and banquet halls sit in a wooded valley.
new.tip: About 14 km from Milas up a mountain road; hours roughly 8:30 to 17:00 and entry may be free, so check. Cooler than the coast in summer.
new.q: Labraunda Antik Kenti, Kıyıcak Köyü, Milas, Muğla

new.title: See the harbour city of Iasos at Kıyıkışlacık
new.desc: Iasos was a Carian and Greek harbour city on a peninsula, with a monumental Roman tomb and finds in the Iasos museum. It sits by the fishing village of Kıyıkışlacık west of Milas.
new.tip: An official museum listing showed it closed at one point, so confirm it is open before the 26 km drive from Milas.
new.q: Iasos Antik Kenti, Kıyıkışlacık Mahallesi, Milas, Muğla

new.title: Climb Beçin Castle above Milas
new.desc: Beçin was the seat of the Menteşe beys and has a fortress on a rock outcrop, 6 km south of Milas on the Ören road. Ruined Turkish bath and mosque remains sit below the walls.
new.tip: Open about 8:00 to 18:30 in summer. Dolmuşes run to Beçin village from Milas; the final stretch is steep.
new.q: Beçin Kalesi, Beçin Mahallesi, Milas, Muğla

new.title: Look inside the Gümüşkesen tomb in Milas
new.desc: This late 2nd-century Roman tomb has Corinthian columns carrying a pyramidal roof and may echo the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus. Visitors can enter the burial chamber.
new.tip: It stands at the edge of Milas, easy to see on foot or by taxi; a short stop of 20 minutes.
new.q: Gümüşkesen Anıt Mezarı, Milas, Muğla

new.title: Browse finds from Iasos and Beçin in the Milas Museum
new.desc: The Milas Museum holds finds from Iasos, Beçin and surrounding Carian sites. It sits opposite the Ulu Camii in the old centre.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, roughly 9:00 to 17:00; closed Mondays.
new.q: Milas Müzesi, Milas, Muğla

new.title: See the 1378 Ulu Camii of Milas
new.desc: Milas's Great Mosque dates to 1378 and is a plain brick Menteşe-era building with a small turret instead of a tall minaret. It anchors the old town beside the museum.
new.tip: Dress modestly; combine with the museum and the Milas bazaar.
new.q: Milas Ulu Camii, Milas, Muğla

new.title: Take a boat to Kara Ada and its hot spring cave
new.desc: Daily cruises run about 30 minutes from Bodrum to Kara Ada, where a volcanic rock cave holds warm thermal water of about 28 to 32 degrees and mineral mud. Tours usually add swim stops in bays such as Rabbit Bay.
new.tip: Full-day trips with lunch start around 10:00 from the harbour; May, June and September are quieter than peak summer.
new.q: Bodrum Marina, Neyzen Tevfik Cd., Merkez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Swim and windsurf at Gümbet Beach
new.desc: Gümbet is a shallow bay 3 km west of Bodrum, safe for paddling and popular for water sports, and a Blue Flag beach. Its Sunday market also sells local produce.
new.tip: Dolmuşes from Bodrum take minutes. Quieter in the morning; evenings bring the bar strip.
new.q: Gümbet Plajı, Gümbet, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Windsurf or swim in the shallows at Bitez
new.desc: Bitez is the top windsurfing spot on the peninsula, with calm shallow water that suits families and mandarin orchards behind the shore. It is a Blue Flag public beach.
new.tip: Wind rises in the afternoon; hire boards on the beach. Mornings are best for swimming.
new.q: Bitez Plajı, Atatürk Bulvarı, Bitez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Float in the clear water at Yahşi Beach, Ortakent
new.desc: Yahşi and Ortakent have clear warm water that suits families and weaker swimmers, and are known for water sports. Ortakent's Wednesday market is nearby.
new.tip: Parking is easiest before 10:00 in peak summer. Dolmuşes run from Bodrum bus station.
new.q: Yahşi Plajı, Ortakent, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Spend a beach day under the pines at Torba
new.desc: Torba has a sandy shore shaded by pines and trees, with the sea deepening gradually. Several large hotels line the bay east of Bodrum.
new.tip: The sea can get rough in the evening, so swim earlier. A dolmuş from Bodrum takes about 15 minutes.
new.q: Torba Plajı, Torba, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Swim in the sheltered Karaincir Bay
new.desc: Karaincir lies in a bay closed on three sides by pine-covered hills, beside the old fishing village of Akyarlar. The water is calm and cool, and the setting quieter than the resort beaches.
new.tip: About 40 minutes by dolmuş from Bodrum via Turgutreis. Akyarlar next door gets the wind for surfing and looks across to Kos.
new.q: Karaincir Belediye Plajı, Akyarlar Mahallesi, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Stroll Yalıkavak Marina at dusk
new.desc: Yalıkavak Marina has about 620 berths for yachts up to 135 m, plus shops, restaurants and a large mooring basin. It fills with strollers in the evening.
new.tip: Evenings are very busy; try early dusk, then walk back through the old village.
new.q: Yalıkavak Marina, Yalıkavak, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Shop the Thursday market in Yalıkavak
new.desc: The weekly Yalıkavak pazarı sells herbs, clothing, local barbun fish and fruit picked that day. Each Bodrum village has its own market day.
new.tip: Thursday mornings are best before the crowd; sources disagree on days, so confirm locally.
new.q: Yalıkavak Pazarı, Plaj Cd., Yalıkavak, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Browse Turgutreis' Saturday market
new.desc: The Turgutreis pazarı runs on Saturdays with herbs, vegetables and fruit, including local Bodrum mandarins in season.
new.tip: Go in the morning; it ends around mid-afternoon.
new.q: Turgutreis Pazar Yeri, Turgutreis, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Pick Bodrum mandarins at the December festival in Bitez
new.desc: The Bodrum Mandarin Festival is held in Bitez in mid-December and opens with a traditional harvest at the municipal demonstration orchard. The green early harvest in autumn is used for juice, while ripe fruit carries a Bodrum geographical indication.
new.tip: The 17th festival was on 15 December 2024; check the municipality for the date. Buy bags at local markets afterwards.
new.q: Bitez Köy Meydanı, Bitez Mahallesi, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Walk the Türkbükü boardwalk
new.desc: Göltürkbükü is a small bay with a semicircular boardwalk of shops, restaurants and piers, long a favourite of Istanbul's elite. There is no broad sandy beach; daytime is spent on jetties.
new.tip: It is pricey; walk the bay at sunset rather than book a lounger.
new.q: Göltürkbükü Sahil, Göltürkbükü, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Swim at the village bay of Gündoğan
new.desc: Gündoğan sits between Yalıkavak and Göltürkbükü and is considered the oldest settlement on the peninsula. It is quieter and cheaper than its neighbours, with swimmable beaches.
new.tip: Walk to the fishing jetty for a village-style lunch afterwards.
new.q: Gündoğan Plajı, Gündoğan, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat grilled octopus and tuna at Orfoz
new.desc: Orfoz in Kumbahçe is a fish restaurant known for sardine sashimi, sea snails, grilled octopus and bluefin tuna.
new.tip: Mid to high prices; reserve in summer.
new.q: Orfoz, Zeki Müren Cd. No:13/1, Kumbahçe, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Order artichoke hearts at Müdavim meyhane by the castle
new.desc: Müdavim is a seaside meyhane near the castle in the Çarşı, known for artichoke hearts and stuffed vegetables.
new.tip: Reservations are needed on summer evenings.
new.q: Müdavim Meyhane, Cumhuriyet Caddesi No:46/1, Çarşı Mahallesi, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat at Dereköy Lokantası in the Bodrum hills
new.desc: Dereköy Lokantası is a garden restaurant on Dereköy Caddesi serving Turkish and modern cooking, listed in the Michelin Guide.
new.tip: Check opening hours before the trip; it is a short drive inland from Gümüşlük.
new.q: Dereköy Lokantası, Dereköy Caddesi No:133, Dereköy, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat Bodrum's çökertme kebabı at Otantik Ocakbaşı
new.desc: Çökertme kebabı is Bodrum's signature dish: thin beef over crisp potato strips with garlic yogurt and tomato sauce, named perhaps after Çökertme village in Milas. Otantik Ocakbaşı has served it for more than 25 years.
new.tip: Sit under the canopy in the garden; mid prices.
new.q: Otantik Ocakbaşı, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Dine at Mimoza on the old stone pier in Gümüşlük
new.desc: Mimoza sits by the old pier and is known for mussel kokoreç dolma, butter shrimp and Turkish coffee served with almond paste and liqueur.
new.tip: Book for sunset; prices are high-mid.
new.q: Mimoza Restaurant, Yalı Mevkii, Gümüşlük, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat grilled octopus at Fenerci in Gümüşlük
new.desc: Fenerci is a relaxed lantern-lit fish restaurant in Gümüşlük serving octopus meze and Aegean starters at fairly affordable prices.
new.tip: Easier to get a table than neighbours; try the octopus.
new.q: Fenerci Restaurant, Kültür Sokak No:3/2, Gümüşlük, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Have breakfast or sunset meze at Limon Gümüşlük
new.desc: Limon is a garden terrace on the hill above Gümüşlük with village breakfast of cheeses, jams and olives, and sunset views over Rabbit Island.
new.tip: Reservation needed at sunset; mid prices.
new.q: Limon Gümüşlük, Kardak Cd., Karakaya Mah., Gümüşlük, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat crispy shrimp at Memedof in Yalıkavak
new.desc: Memedof is a seafront fish restaurant on Çökertme Cd. known for crispy shrimp, stuffed zucchini flowers and daily fish.
new.tip: Mid to high prices; ask for the day's catch by weight.
new.q: Memedof Balık Restaurant, Çökertme Caddesi No:42, Yalıkavak, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Try grilled squid with thyme at Garo's
new.desc: Garo's is a stylish seaside restaurant in Göltürkbükü popular with celebrities, known for grilled squid with mountain thyme.
new.tip: High prices; book in summer.
new.q: Garo's Restaurant, Türkbükü Sahil, Göltürkbükü Mahallesi, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat fresh fish and meze at Atılay Balık in Göltürkbükü
new.desc: Atılay Balık on Liman Caddesi serves fresh fish and a wide meze selection beside the bay.
new.tip: Mid to high prices; fish is priced by weight.
new.q: Atılay Balık Restaurant, Liman Caddesi No:81/B, Göltürkbükü, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Lunch on local-cooperative fish at Terzi Mustafa'nın Yeri
new.desc: Terzi Mustafa'nın Yeri in Gündoğan serves fish from the local cooperative and a village breakfast.
new.tip: Mid prices; a good village alternative to Türkbükü.
new.q: Terzi Mustafa'nın Yeri, Gündoğan, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Pick your fish and eat it at Rota Balık in Turgutreis
new.desc: Rota Balık is a fish restaurant in Turgutreis known for its starters; guests choose fish at a nearby fishmonger and have it cooked to order.
new.tip: Ask about the cooking fee when you bring fish from the shop.
new.q: Rota Balık, Turgutreis, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat crispy mantı and liver at Bağarası, Bitez
new.desc: Bağarası in Bitez is a meyhane with daily meze, crispy mantı, liver and çöp şiş.
new.tip: Reserve in the evening; mid prices.
new.q: Bağarası, Bitez, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Try kavurma and meze at Tahta Meyhane in Dereköy
new.desc: Tahta Meyhane in Dereköy near Gümüşlük serves liver, kavurma and meze in a former oil mill.
new.tip: Evening only; mid prices.
new.q: Tahta Meyhane, Dereköy Caddesi No:160, Dereköy, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Eat home-style Aegean vegetables at Kısmet Lokantası
new.desc: Kısmet Lokantası in Konacık is a lunch-time esnaf lokantası serving Aegean vegetable dishes and böreks.
new.tip: Cheap; lunch only, arrive early.
new.q: Kısmet Lokantası, Konacık, Bodrum, Muğla

new.title: Have a garden breakfast with home-made jams at Asmalı Çardak
new.desc: Asmalı Çardak in Yalıkavak serves breakfast with home-made jams and börek from produce grown on site.
new.tip: Breakfast and brunch; mid prices.
new.q: Asmalı Çardak, Kayacık Caddesi No:52, Yalıkavak, Bodrum, Muğla
